title: Progressive Deploy Strategies — Console UX & Wireframe Notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact UX-oriented set of notes, quick wireframe descriptions, and groomed backlog tasks for the Progressive Deploy / Rollouts area of the Console. Focus: designing an operator-friendly surface for canaries, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies that plays well with Dedicated/Private deployments and the hosted API.

Design goals (high level):
- Make common progressive patterns (canary, A/B, traffic shifts) discoverable and fast to configure.
- Surface risk signals and quick rollback actions at a glance.
- Enable repeatable, policy-driven fallbacks that degrade gracefully by model variant, region, or capacity tier.
- Keep the new flow keyboard-friendly and accessible; compact for frequent retriggers.

Primary user flows described:
1) Create a Canary (quick path)
   - Entry points: model page > "New rollout" button or route configuration > "Add experiment".
   - Quick path fields: name, target route, baseline model, candidate model, percentage to candidate (slider default 5%), duration window (default 30m), success metric (latency P95 or request error rate).
   - Microcopy: "Start small — monitor for 30m. You can pause or rollback instantly."
   - Wireframe notes: single-column modal with inline metric selector showing three small sparklines: 1) request rate, 2) error rate, 3) P95 latency. A compact preview line reads: "Candidate: gptx-2q (quantized) — expected latency +10% — recommended for cost-sensitive batches."
   - Acceptance criteria (quick path): must create rollout, route 5% traffic to candidate, show real-time metric delta during window, provide immediate pause and rollback action buttons.

2) A/B Group Editor (advanced)
   - Use case: multi-variant experiments (n>2) with allocation and custom routing rules.
   - Editor layout: two-pane. Left: variants list (drag to reorder). Right: allocation table, per-variant filters (region, user segment tag), and golden metrics.
   - Variant filters: allow "header matcher" and "tenant id prefix" so platform teams can test for specific customers.
   - Acceptance criteria: can create >2 variants, apply allocation percentages that sum to 100%, and persist per-variant rollout policies (e.g., warm-up, burst capacity).

3) Fallback Policy Builder (policy-driven automatic fallbacks)
   - Motivation: avoid manual hotfixes when a model degrades or a region loses capacity.
   - Builder canvas: node-based visual where each node is a condition (metric threshold, error explosion, capacity signal) and edges point to actions (step down to variant, route to other region, reduce batch size, or fallback to cached response).
   - Simple DSL preview: show the equivalent text policy for the visual graph, editable inline. Example DSL snippet shown in the UI preview: "when p50_latency > 1200ms for 3m then route -> fallback-variant-1 for 10m; if error_rate > 5% escalate -> route -> region-secondary".
   - Wireframe: canvas with palette (conditions, timers, actions). Compact breadcrumb at top: Service > Model > Policy name > last-saved.
   - Acceptance criteria: user can save a policy, attach it to an active rollout, and simulate the policy against historical telemetry (simulate mode).

Telemetry / Observability integration notes:
- Show both absolute and delta metrics against baseline. Metric cards: Req/s, Error %, P50/P95, Cost per 1k tokens. Each card has a small dropdown for time window and cohort filters (region/tenant).
- Add a "Signal severity" indicator (green/yellow/red) computed from normalized z-score of the metric vs baseline. Provide hover tooltip explaining the calculation.
- Important: metric latency windows must match the rollout window. E.g., a 30m canary should default to 15/30/60 minute breakdown.

Wireframe interactions / microcopy details:
- Pause vs Rollback: Pause preserves allocation but stops traffic changes; Rollback actively reassigns traffic back to baseline. Buttons: [Pause rollout] (secondary), [Rollback now] (danger).
- Quick insight badges next to model names: e.g., "compacts-quant" (icon) with tooltip: "~2.2x CPU savings; verify parity on open-domain QA".
- Inline warnings for incompatible model variants (different vocab size / unsupported ops) with link: "Compatibility guide".

Backlog (groomed items, scoped, prioritized):
- B-101: Add DSL "simulate" run: replay last 12h of traffic against a fallback policy. (est 3 spikes)
- B-102: Accessibility pass for rollout modal (keyboard order, ARIA labels, color contrast). (est 2 spikes)
- B-103: Telemetry deltas: implement P95 delta bar and z-score to severity mapping. (est 5 spikes)
- B-104: Add tenant-scoped filters for A/B editor and per-variant sticky routing for sessions. (est 4 spikes)
- B-105: Integrate cost-per-1k token metric for candidate vs baseline and show projected monthly delta. (est 3 spikes)
- B-106: Create default templates: "Risk-averse Canary" (1% -> 5% -> 15% over 2h), "Performance-first" (50% warm-up). (est 2 spikes)
- B-107: Safety net: automatic rollback when 3 critical signals trip within 10 minutes. Expose threshold config in advanced panel. (est 4 spikes)

Edge cases and unresolved questions (for discussion in grooming):
- Sticky sessions: if a user is routed to candidate during rollout, should they remain for the life of session? (pros: consistent behavior; cons: lingering errors). Proposed default: sticky for 5 minutes, configurable per rollout.
- Multi-region fallbacks: if region-secondary lacks variant, should the system route to baseline model in that region or to hosted cross-region pool? Need infra input for latency SLA impact.
- Canary metrics for low-volume routes: need statistical heuristics to avoid noisy decisions. Proposed: warn and extend window or block automatic promotion.

Sample keyboard flow (for accessibility):
- Open rollout modal (Enter on focused route) -> Tab to name -> Tab to variant selector (type-to-search) -> Tab to percentage slider (arrow keys to adjust) -> Tab to duration -> Tab to metric selector -> Enter Start.

Error and recovery states to design for:
- Failure creating rollout: show actionable error with link to relevant quota/permission docs when the error is 403/429.
- Partial rollout failure (some regions failed to accept allocation): highlight affected regions in table and offer per-region retry.
- Policy save conflict: warn if attached rollout is active and propose save-as-new option.

Mock grant matrix for rollout actions (notes for SSO/RBAC):
- rollout:create: project-editors and above.
- rollout:pause/rollback: project-operators and above.
- rollout:attach-policy: project-operators.

Next steps / immediate experiments:
- Build clickable prototype for the quick-canary modal (Figma), test with two customers in next week (SRE and internal platform team).
- Spike: telemetry deltas calculation (2 days) to validate UI thresholds.
- Host a 45-minute design review with infra and SRE to align multi-region fallback semantics.

Notes and references:
- See linked Confluence doc for policy DSL rationale.
- Related Jira: JIRA-PI-3421 (Rollout infra changes), Github PR for frontend explorations linked above.

Author notes (Aisha):
- Intentionally kept default canary allocations conservative. We should provide one-click templates to reduce cognitive load.
- Prioritize a small-surface quick path and a richer advanced editor; many customers will use quick path 80% of the time.

End of document.
